claim:annealing.proposition: Bulk <n> converges to ~5.97 within ~2 MCS with total<bulk, reproducing Fig 2; cell walls compact by 2-20 MCS (Fig 3).
claim:annealing.hypothesis: Two MCS of T=0 annealing removes crumpling and disconnected spins, bringing bulk <n> within ~0.2% of its ~6.0 limit.

primary_tests.name: Topological equilibrium under T=0 annealing
primary_tests.pass_if: final ⟨n⟩_bulk ≈ 6 (within 0.3) and μ₂ decreases while annealing

claim:global_equilibration.proposition: The tiling rounds into a 1012-cell disk with <n>~6.0, mu2~0.69, matching Fig 4b; statistics stable after ~400 MCS (Fig 5).
claim:global_equilibration.hypothesis: After 400 MCS the tiling rounds into a disk with <n>~6.04, mu2~0.69, a stable shared initial condition.

primary_tests.name: Brick tiling rounds to a disk at topological equilibrium

evidence_refs: Brick tiling rounds to a disk at topological equilibrium

claim:checkerboard.proposition: gamma_ld<0 yields a defect-ridden checkerboard with dominant light-dark contact and two transitions (~T=0 freeze, ~T=15 mixing), matching Figs 7-9 and Table I.
claim:checkerboard.hypothesis: Cells maximize heterotypic contact, so the light-dark fractional interface dominates and remains high; defects persist by thermal activation.

primary_tests.name: Heterotypic contacts dominate (checkerboard mixing)
primary_tests.pass_if: light-dark fraction > 0.5 and larger than light-light & dark-dark

claim:cell_sorting.proposition: Complete cell sorting: dark cells cluster internally beneath a light monolayer; heterotypic contact falls while light-medium contact rises, reproducing Figs 12-16 and Tables II-III.
claim:cell_sorting.hypothesis: Low-surface-energy dark cells coalesce internally while light cells form an outer monolayer; surface sorting slows logarithmically.

primary_tests.name: Cells sort: dark cluster wrapped by a light monolayer
primary_tests.pass_if: light-dark fraction falls ≥45% AND light holds >80% of the medium surface (monolayer)

evidence_refs: Cells sort: dark cluster wrapped by a light monolayer

claim:engulfment.proposition: Light cells engulf the dark mass and the final state matches the random-IC sort, confirming initial-condition independence (Figs 18-19).
claim:engulfment.hypothesis: Global energy minimization drives light to engulf dark independent of initial condition; engulfment is slow (~10^4 MCS).

primary_tests.name: Light engulfs the coherent dark mass (no mixing)
primary_tests.pass_if: light-dark stays low (<0.20, no mixing) AND dark-medium falls ≥80% AND light owns >85% of the surface

evidence_refs: Light engulfs the coherent dark mass (no mixing)

claim:position_reversal.proposition: Dark cells sort OUTWARD, surrounding the light cells, the reversed pattern predicted for gamma_lM>gamma_dM (Figs 20-21).
claim:position_reversal.hypothesis: With gamma_lM >> gamma_dM the dark cells present the lower medium tension and form the outer layer, giving a reversed pattern.

primary_tests.name: Position reversal: dark forms the outer monolayer
primary_tests.pass_if: dark holds >80% of the medium surface (light-Medium→0) AND light-dark contact falls (sorting)

evidence_refs: Position reversal: dark forms the outer monolayer

claim:partial_sorting.proposition: Sorting stalls partial: no light monolayer forms and clusters trap inclusions, markedly slower than normal sorting (Figs 22-24).
claim:partial_sorting.hypothesis: Light cells cannot fully surround dark; clusters trap heterotypic inclusions and never form a monolayer, sorting logarithmically slow.

primary_tests.name: Partial sorting stalls: coarsening but no monolayer
primary_tests.pass_if: light-dark contact drops (coarsening) BUT light never owns the surface — no monolayer (corr_lM<0.75, vs >0.85 for complete sorting)

evidence_refs: Partial sorting stalls: coarsening but no monolayer

claim:dispersal_sloughing.proposition: Light cells disperse as isolated cells into the medium while dark cells remain compact and round (Fig 25).
claim:dispersal_sloughing.hypothesis: Light cells prefer medium contact and detach as isolated cells while dark cells stay compact and round.

primary_tests.name: Light cells slough off and disperse into the medium
primary_tests.pass_if: light-medium fraction rises ≥3× and total boundary length increases (fragmentation)

evidence_refs: Light cells slough off and disperse into the medium

claim:dispersal_separate.proposition: Light and dark clusters separate completely; a few isolated dark cells occur (Fig 26).
claim:dispersal_separate.hypothesis: Extreme heterotypic tension drives complete separation of light and dark clusters, with a few isolated dark cells.

primary_tests.name: Clusters separate (both types expose new medium surface)
primary_tests.pass_if: total boundary length increases and both medium-contact fractions rise

evidence_refs: Clusters separate (both types expose new medium surface)

claim:dispersal_no_separate.proposition: Clusters remain attached, an extreme partial-sorting case just below the separation threshold (Fig 27).
claim:dispersal_no_separate.hypothesis: Just below the separation threshold, clusters remain joined despite strong heterotypic tension.

primary_tests.name: Clusters stay aggregated (no separation)
primary_tests.pass_if: total boundary length does not increase (aggregate stays compact)

evidence_refs: Dispersal — clusters do not separate — interactive

claim:vacancy_cavity.proposition: A light-cell-lined medium cavity nucleates within the aggregate (Fig 28); reproduced approximately (the paper notes this case is delicate).
claim:vacancy_cavity.hypothesis: Relaxing vacancy suppression lets medium nucleate internally, lined by light cells, forming a fluid-filled cavity.

primary_tests.name: Cavity nucleates and rounds; dark accumulates
primary_tests.pass_if: total boundary length decreases (cavity rounds) and dark-dark contact rises

evidence_refs: Cavity nucleates and rounds; dark accumulates

narrative.question: Can a single extended-Potts (Cellular Potts) model with only differential surface energies and an area constraint reproduce the full range of differential-adhesion-driven cell-rearrangement phenomena reported by Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993)?
